source.title: Language Model Activations Inhabit Privileged Error-Correcting Basins
source.authors: Matthew Finlayson; Francisco Pernice; Eric Todd; Amir Zur; Daniel Wurgaft; Fenil R. Doshi; Vasudev Shyam; Matt Feiszli; Satchel Grant; Lucius Bushnaq; Tal Haklay; Usha Bhalla; Matthew Kowal; Thomas Fel; Jack Merullo; Atticus Geiger; Xiang Ren; Owen Lewis; E. Lubana

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses error-correcting dynamics and reports its own activation-geometry results, but it does not test component ablation or whether downstream components restore an original prediction.
record.gate_note: No attention layer or head is ablated, and the paper does not compare a component's direct effect with the final output effect. Its synthetic-activation norm-growth results are related to error correction but do not measure the ablation-based behavior in the claim versions. Cited results from the original sources are background only.
record.test_reason: The paper probes activation-space geometry (norm growth, speed profiles of spherical probes) and steering between basins. It ablates no attention layer, head or MLP to measure downstream compensation of the output, so its results do not bear on any self-repair version. The original sources are cited only as background on error correction. Its 'context ablation' keeps only the BOS token to isolate feedforward layers; it is a method choice, not a test of compensation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that natural activations occupy a cluster of distinct attracting, error-correcting basins that separate them from synthetic activations (AUROC up to 0.997). They hold that steering moves activations between feature basins, and that basin-aware adaptive steering beats fixed-strength English-to-Chinese steering. They make no claim about component-ablation compensation.
record.recipe_differences: No component-ablation method or ablation-based output-effect measure is used.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported synthetic-activation norm-growth trajectory differs by activation type and forward-pass stage: norm-matched activations begin with high growth and then approach natural growth, while shuffled activations eventually reach a local maximum.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic activations injected at a layer shift toward natural-activation per-block norm growth over later blocks in Llama 3.1 8B (also OLMo and Qwen, Fig. 14). Authors read this as distributed error correction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Later transformer blocks move off-distribution residual activations toward natural-activation geometry (activation-level error correction).

fits_no_version.finding: Re-initialized probes show norm-matched activations entering a norm-growth basin quickly, while shuffled ones later reach a local maximum like natural activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different synthetic activation classes are pulled into natural-like attracting basins at different rates.

record.problems: For the claim here, the evidence is indirect: it uses synthetic activations and norm-growth geometry rather than component ablations and output predictions. The relevant trajectory descriptions are qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: Refusal and language-steering findings were not extracted because they do not test ablation compensation or the restoration of an original prediction.

untested.parts: No attention-layer ablation or measurement of later-layer compensation of the output.
No late-MLP erasure measurement and no ablation of earlier components.
No single-head ablation on general text.
No per-prompt compensation distribution and no overcorrection test.
No backup heads, copy-suppression, LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons are examined.
No mean or resample ablation compared with zero ablation.
No ablation-based importance scores are compared with direct effects.

record.verdict_notes: The four rows' 'partial' states were set against no version, so they are recast as cannot_determine with versions none. Refusal, language-steering and AUROC results were correctly left out as unrelated to self-repair. The text contains no instructions aimed at the reader.

versions.untested_parts: No attention-layer ablation or later-layer compensation on the output prediction.
No late-MLP erasure or earlier-component ablation.
No attention-head ablation or full-distribution compensation test.
No ablation-compensation measurements across prompts or test of overcorrection.
No test of backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as ablation-repair mechanisms.
No on-distribution ablation using mean or resample ablation.
No ablation-based importance score or comparison with a component's direct effect.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses prior self-repair findings as evidence of error correction, without testing or operationally using component-ablation compensation.

tranche.reason: Activation geometry and steering measure a related construct; no result measures compensation following component ablation or tests another listed self-repair version.

source_check.notes: The study ablates context in selected experiments, rather than model components to measure compensation. These qualitative norm-growth results cannot determine any listed self-repair version.
